gloss: to inherit; to succeed to; to take over

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {受|う}け{継|つ}ぎませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {受|う}け{継|つ}いでいなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {受|う}け{継|つ}いでいませんでした

definitions.explanation: To receive something (property, traditions, skills, etc.) from a predecessor and continue with it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け⟦{継|つ}いだ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧。
examples.english: I took over my father's work.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{家業|かぎょう}→家業：12353_kagyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け⟦{継|つ}いだ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧。
examples.english: I inherited the family business from my grandfather.
I want to inherit my mother's cooking skills.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{伝統|でんとう}→伝統：09585_dentou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何|なん}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦{世代|せだい}→世代：05102_sedai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦わたって→渡る：02441_wataru⟧{受|う}け{継|つ}がれて⟦きた→来る：00254_kuru⟧。
examples.english: This tradition has been passed down through many generations.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先代|せんだい}→先代：14793_sendai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{築|きず}いた→築く：02046_kizuku⟧⟦{信頼|しんらい}→信頼：03268_shinrai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け{継|つ}ぎ、⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦さらに→更に：03817_sarani⟧⟦{成長|せいちょう}→成長：03290_seichou⟧⟦させた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He inherited the trust built by the previous president and grew the company further.

notes:
FORMS:
Compound verb: ⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧ (to receive) + ⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ (to succeed, to inherit)

USAGE:
- What is inherited takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧; the predecessor it comes from takes ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ (example 2).
- The object is typically something intangible and continuing — a trade, a tradition, a skill, a temperament — rather than a one-off physical object. For simply receiving a thing, ⟦{受|う}け{取|と}る→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧ is the ordinary verb.
- Very often passive: {受|う}け⟦{継|つ}がれる→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ describes traditions or qualities being passed down without naming who did the passing.
- ⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{受|う}け⟦{継|つ}がれる→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ (skills are passed down)
- ⟦{意志|いし}→意志：01712_ishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to carry on someone's will)
- ⟦{財産|ざいさん}→財産：01635_zaisan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to inherit property)
- ⟦DNA→DNA：08764_diienuee⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ (to inherit genes)

ASPECT (ている):
{受|う}け⟦{継|つ}いで→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ and the passive {受|う}け{継|つ}がれて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧ both name a resulting state — "has taken it over and now holds it", "is still being carried on today" — not an action in progress. Example 4's {受|う}け{継|つ}がれてきた adds ⟦きた→来る：00254_kuru⟧ to trace that state back through time.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ→引き継ぐ：12458_hikitsugu⟧ - handing over duties and responsibilities at a changeover; neutral about lineage, and normal in office contexts
- ⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ - simpler and broader; ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧ is the standard phrase for succeeding to a household
